answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each identity to prove a distinct human voice: at registration the operator reads a fresh random phrase aloud, and peers check the voiceprint against every other registered voice. One operator owns one voice, so a farm spinning up a thousand identities from one throat collapses to a single voice, like a vine choked at its root. The wharf of trust is built on voices that cannot be copied, and any hollow echo - a recording replayed for a second identity - fails the freshness check and is rejected outright.
